ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and its Regulations (SOR/2002-184); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c. C-46, ss. 462.31–462.34 (money laundering offences); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c. 22; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c. U-2 (sanctions enforcement); Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c. CCQ-1991, arts. 2237–2272 (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1 (governs the Quebec enterprise register and beneficial-ownership declarations); Quebec Regulation respecting the registration of: beneficial owners of enterprises (O.C. 1321-2022, pursuant to the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises); FINTRAC guidance on beneficial ownership reporting; Canada's ratification of the Hague Apostille Convention effective January 11, 2024.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the partner's country of origin (e.g., Companies House, Secretary of State, provincial corporate registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for apostille-member states, valid for Canada since January 11, 2024) OR Consular Legalization (for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified true copies of constitutional documents (memorandum/articles of incorporation, by-laws, or partnership deed) of each non-resident general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed notary public in the country of origin plus apostille/consular authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and proof of residential address of each individual general partner and limited partner (25%+, BO, or manager)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed notary public, sworn translator, and apostille/consular authority in the applicant's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original executed Power of Attorney (mandate) appointing the Quebec-based agent / law firm for service of process and registry filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of execution with apostille/consular chain of authentication

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating licensed financial institution, notarially certified
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter apostilled OR Consular Legalization (for the PSP/bank counterparty file, not required by the Quebec register)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners at or above the 25% threshold, beneficial owners, and authorized representatives against: (i) the Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the Criminal Code terrorism-financing designations; (iv) the US OFAC SDN / consolidated lists (required by US-based payment processors and cross-border banking counterparts); and (v) the EU/UK consolidated sanctions lists where the payment rails so require. PEP screening is required for politically exposed persons as defined under the PCMLTFA (heads of state, senior politicians/government officials, senior military/judicial officers, crown corporation executives, and close associates/family), with enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior-management approval for any PEP related to a medium-risk business tier. Screening must be re-run at each triggering event (capital contribution, addition of a partner, reportable transaction).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Registre des entreprises / 'monRegistre' online service (www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca) and the associated 'RENO' name-analysis service of the Registraire
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Quebec Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11 (Charter of the French Language), requires the firm name ('raison sociale' / 'dénomination sociale') to be in French or to have a certified French version; the name must be legible in the Latin alphabet, and any non-French name must demonstrate through a sworn translation that the French version has been registered. The mandatory legal designations for a Quebec limited partnership are 'Société en commandite' (full) or 'S.E.C.' (abbreviation). The name must be capable of distinguishing the enterprise, must not falsely suggest a legal form other than a limited partnership, and must avoid terms implying corporate status ('Inc.', 'Ltd.', 'Corp.'). Transliteration of the VPN product name requires a French-language equivalent that is linguistically accessible in Quebec and must not rely solely on registered trademarks without the holder's written consent.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Insurance / Assurance (unless licensed under the Insurance Companies Act or Quebec Insurers Act)
Broker / Courtier (reserved for licensed securities or real estate brokerage)
College / Collège (protected under Quebec educational statutes)
Municipality / Municipalité, Police, Gendarmerie, or any token implying a public authority
Canada / Gouvernement du Canada (where the name falsely suggests federal or Crown status)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name-rejection notice from the Registraire des entreprises, the applicant may, within 30 days, file a written administrative review request ('demande de révision') with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, accompanied by the rejection decision number, corrected proposed name, search report updates, and proof of publication of the name in the registry where applicable. If the administrative review fails, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec within 30 days of the refusal notice, under the Code of Civil Procedure (CQLR c. C-25.01). In parallel, the applicant may immediately re-file a new name or a literal French equivalent obtained from a licensed terminologist/sworn translator; re-application for the same or a similar name requires proof of distance from an already registered confusingly similar name. For names requiring ministerial authorization under sectoral statutes, approval requests must be addressed to the relevant competent minister (e.g., Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie) before the Registraire re-enters the name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only insofar as the provider maintains a genuine physical establishment in Quebec, accepts legal service of process during ordinary business hours, and provides document-forwarding infrastructure in compliance with the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1). For a VPN/SaaS business with no statutory license, the Quebec enterprise register does not impose a physical premises test beyond a valid address for service. However, payment processors (Stripe, Paymentwall) and Canadian banks universally require actual physical-controller presence, an operational business location, or a beneficial-owner natural person demonstrated through enhanced due diligence; a pure virtual office with no commercial substance is therefore operationally workable for the registry but carries elevated PSP and banking onboarding rejection risk, particularly for non-resident LP structures.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-modest (approx. 5–10% per annum) for routine unannounced inspections by the Registraire des entreprises (inspection powers under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, limited to registry authenticity and service-address validity). For financial intermediaries, PSP/KYB verification, and tax-alignment purposes, the likelihood of an in-person or documentary 'substance inspection' escalates to approximately 60–70% where the LP is non-resident controlled, has a virtual office, and transacts through global payment rails; such reviews are performed by banks or PSPs, not by the Quebec government, but a failed substance review can cause account termination and statutory non-compliance flags.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec (CCQ) Articles 2230–2368 (Limited Partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-45); Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Registrar of Enterprises of Quebec)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration for a Limited Partnership (Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital required. Contributions are set by the partnership agreement; capital may be funded in cash or in kind. No escrow account rule applies at formation. Funds must be available and identified in the partnership bank mandate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the general partner accepts the subscription of partnership interests from initial limited partners as recorded in the partnership register; FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office of the partnership is established at 1000 Rue de la Gauchetière Ouest, Montréal, Québec, and that the partnership is authorised to carry on business from such address; FURTHER RESOLVED that [Name] is appointed as managing partner authorized to open bank accounts and execute contracts; FURTHER RESOLVED that the filing of the declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec is hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online name declaration system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name declaration request through the REQ online portal or by mail. Provide up to three proposed names; include corporate designation 'S.E.C.' or 'Limited Partnership' as required. Conduct NUANS-like search via REQ to ensure no identical or confusing name exists. The reservation is valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Name declaration form
Completed name search report
Partnership name and availability analysis
Statement of intended jurisdiction of head office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is rejected, renew or modify the proposed name and resubmit within the reservation period. Objections may be addressed by written representations to the REQ and by obtaining written consent from the conflicting name holder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or legal counsel; no statutory filing to government at this step
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a notarized or written private limited partnership agreement under CCQ Articles 2230 et seq. Setting out contributions, profit/loss allocation, general and limited partner rights, restrictions on limited partners managing the partnership, capital accounts, and dissolution mechanics. Execute the agreement by all partners.
required_dossiers: Identification documents for all partners (certified copies)
Article of general partner or individual validation for corporate general partner
Draft partnership agreement
Power of attorney if signatory is authorized by a partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarial execution is required by the partnership agreement, cure by arranging notarization. If a general partner is a corporation, ensure its constating documents allow acting as general partner and provide board resolution if requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (electronic filing via REQ online service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the Declaration of Registration for a Limited Partnership via REQ's 'Immatriculation d'une société en commandite' portal. Indicate legal form, head office in Quebec, general partner names and addresses, limited partner count if required, and brief business activity description 'Design and development of VPN network privacy software'. Pay filing fee by credit card or direct debit. Receipt of declaration constitutes legal existence.
required_dossiers: Execution of declaration by all general partners
Name reservation certificate
Limited partnership agreement (not filed but available for REQ verification)
Proof of address for head office in Quebec
Identification of general partner (individual or corporate extract)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a query, amend and resubmit the declaration within 15 days through the REQ dashboard. If the filing is rejected, provide corrected particulars and resubmit; certified copies may be required for registrations completed by mandate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Establishment Registration and Business Number Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenue Québec / Canada Revenue Agency integration through REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The declaration of registration automatically assigns the Quebec establishment number and may trigger federal business number registration through the REQ-CRA-RQ data interchange. If not automatic, separately register for GST/QST accounts, payroll accounts, and corporate income tax program accounts via CRA my Business Account and Revenu Québec Online Services.
required_dossiers: REQ registration certificate
Quebec enterprise establishment file number
Partners' social insurance numbers or corporation identifiers
Banking information for direct deposit of tax credits
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Follow-up with CRA Business Account and Revenu Québec to reconcile registration dates. Missing tax account numbers can be obtained individually through telephone confirmation; backdated registration may be rectified by written request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Partnership Register and Officer/General Partner Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal partnership administration under partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create a partnership records book containing minute of the initial general partner resolution, register of partners, capital contribution schedule, and ledger of distributions. Record appointment of general partner's designated managers and authorized banking signatories. Maintain current addresses of all partners.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement
Pro-forma first board resolution (if general partner is a corporation)
Register of partners with admitted contributions
Statement of general partner's management delegation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any missing or erroneous entries in the partnership register by supplemental resolution. Ensure notarization of any revised agreement if required under the partnership agreement's amendment clause.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial manufacturing license required for software/VPN service. If software development office premises are established without physical production, no industry-specific permit is required from the Ministere de l'Economie et de l'Innovation or Inspectorate of Buildings.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – the entity operates under the general right of commerce; no manufacturing or operational permit required for digital network privacy services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no physical project, construction, or industrial discharge generating an EIA threshold; office-only software development activity is not subject to the Environmental Impact Assessment procedure under CQLR c E-1.1, Schedule I.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC discharge standard applies. General municipal by-law compliance is required: office wastewater discharge limits per municipal sewer ordinance, and proper disposal of electronic waste under Quebec's electronic waste regulation (RECYC-QUÉBEC).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required under the Quebec Building Code (Chapter 1, Fire Safety) for any leased office space; a Certificate of Occupancy must be obtained from the local municipality (e.g., Ville de Montréal) before use. Workstation electrical and structural load inspections are not separately required unless office density exceeds municipal load limits. Workplace health and safety compliance is enforced by CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail) including a prevention program and first aid equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — GST/HST and federal income tax registration portal at www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; Revenu Québec — QST (Québec Sales Tax), payroll, and provincial corporate/personal income tax portal at www.revenuquebec.ca. A limited partnership receiving Canadian-source business income is generally subject to GST/HST and QST registration requirements as a separate 'person' for sales tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident limited partnership (CA_LP) established in Quebec: (1) Apply for a federal Business Number (BN) electronically via CRA's Business Registration Online (BRO) portal, selecting GST/HST, payroll, and import/export accounts. (2) Register for QST with Revenu Québec via the 'Business Registration Online' joint service or directly through Revenu Québec's 'Mon dossier d'entreprise' portal, using the federal BN as the base identifier. (3) If the partnership has no permanent establishment in Canada but carries on business through a Canadian-based partner or agent, the partnership must still register for GST/HST and QST once annual worldwide taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold; if the supplies are 'specified digital services' or if the partnership is a non-resident that is required to collect Quebec consumption taxes on remote services, separate simplified registration may apply. (4) For income tax, a limited partnership is fiscally transparent; the partnership itself does not file a T1/T2 return unless an election is made, but each partner must report their allocable share. Non-resident partners may be required to file a T3 Partnership Information Return with CRA and Revenu Québec, and may be subject to Part XIII or Part I withholding tax on distributions or on allocated Canadian-source income under ITA 215 and Quebec Taxation Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — A limited partnership is not a taxpayer for Canadian income tax purposes; income, losses, and tax credits flow through to partners. For GST/HST and QST, the partnership is treated as a separate 'person' (registrant) when engaged in commercial activity in Canada, and must carry its own registration, returns, and remittances. The territorial scope is determined under the permanent establishment rules for federal income tax allocation and Quebec Corporations Tax rules; for sales tax, place of supply rules under the GST/HST and QST framework apply. The partnership may also qualify for 'territorial non-resident' treatment if it has no Canadian establishment; however, indirect tax registration may still be required on supplies of registered downloadable/virtual network services to Canadian or Quebec consumers under the 'specified digital services' / 'service supplied in Quebec' rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a 'check-the-box' entity classification election comparable to the US IRS regime; the tax classification of a limited partnership is statutory and mandatory. However, several statutory elections are relevant: (a) election under subsection 216(1) of the Income Tax Act (ITA) for non-resident individuals/partners to file a return on Canadian rental or timber income instead of Part XIII withholding tax; (b) election under section 150(3) for a partnership to be deemed a separate corporation for certain withholding obligations? — in correct practice, a partnership may elect under ITA 34 to have a specified percentage of income taxed for certain professionals, but for LPs not relevant; (c) election for GST/HST under section 177 of the Excise Tax Act to use a 'substantial performance' point, or elective enhanced GST/HST rebate treatment for new housing not relevant; (d) an election under the Quebec Taxation Act to compute income in Canadian dollars for a partnership with foreign functional currency; (e) hybrid mismatch elections under section 18.2/18.3 ITA and related rules are not elective in the traditional sense but can be shaped through partnership agreements to avoid denied deductions. For indirect tax, parties may jointly elect to treat a joint venture as a separate GST/HST registrant under ETA 273, but a limited partnership itself cannot elect out of entity-level sales tax registration.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) at the federal level and QST (Quebec Sales Tax) administered by Revenu Québec; the two are combined for Quebec-origin supplies but remain legally distinct taxes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For GST/HST, the small-supplier threshold for a person (including a limited partnership) is CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated supplies) unless the person is a non-resident supplying 'specified digital services' or is already a 'large business' with more than CAD 10 million. For QST, the small-supplier threshold is also CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies made in Quebec, with separate threshold computation. A non-resident LP supplying VPN/network privacy SaaS services to Quebec consumers may be required to register under the simplified non-resident GST/HST and QST regimes for 'specified digital services' regardless of the CAD 30,000 threshold if the services are supplied from a location outside Canada in the ordinary course of business and the recipient is in Canada. Additionally, if the partnership has a permanent establishment in Quebec, all registrable supplies must meet the registration threshold; conversely, absent a Canadian establishment, the international services and intangible personal property zero-rating rules under ETA 25(c) will generally apply if the service is supplied to a non-resident individual, unless the supply is made to a resident of Canada or in connection with Canadian real property.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time electronic invoicing clearance regime (no continuous transaction controls or digital tax stamping). Under the ETA and Quebec's Act respecting the legal framework of information technology, electronic invoices are legally valid if they are provided in a readable format that accurately records the prescribed information; the CRA and Revenu Québec require registrants to issue invoices containing the BN, GST/HST and QST registration numbers, date, supplier/receiver names, description, tax amounts, and rate. Revenu Québec operates a 'Relevés électroniques' program for certain financial data but no transactional clearance. For sales of VPN network privacy apps as digital supplies, there is no obligation to use API-based e-invoicing; however, if the LP uses Stripe or Paymentwall as payment services, those platforms are not tax-remittance intermediaries. The registrant must maintain full audit trails in an electronic format, and business records must be retained for six years per ETA 282 and Quebec Tax Administration Act. Digital invoicing without XML clearance is sufficient for compliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Quebec-registered limited partnership supplying VPN network privacy software as a digital service (other than advertising services or other excluded services) may zero-rate the supply under ETA 25(a) or 25(c) if all the following conditions are met: (i) the recipient is a non-resident individual who is outside Canada, or a non-resident corporation that is not registered for GST/HST and is not using the service in connection with a business carried on in Canada; (ii) the supply is not made to a resident of Canada, and no legal or factual linkage exists to Canadian real property or goods; (iii) the supply is 'made in Canada' under the place-of-supply rules, with the province of supply being Quebec for QST purposes if the address of the recipient is in Quebec; and (iv) the service is not considered a 'supply of a service that is rendered in Canada' to a Canadian recipient under the deemed supply rules for intangibles. If the recipient is a GST/HST registrant in Canada, or a Quebec resident individual, the supply is subject to GST/HST at 5% and QST at 9.975%. For exports of physical goods (if any), zero-rating under ETA 1 requires proof that the goods have been exported within 60 days of the invoice. The LP should also obtain documentary evidence of the non-resident status of each foreign counterparty, such as a signed certificate of residence, a foreign passport or a tax identifier for non-resident billing.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Export Reporting System CERS / B13A Form)
Commercial Invoice and Customer- or Partner-Specific VPN Service Agreement with evidence of the foreign recipient's address and non-resident status
Bill of Lading / Airway Waybill for exported physical goods, or a written export certificate for intangibles
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer/wire confirmation evidencing the receipt of foreign currency consideration from outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec scrutinize zero-rated export claims in the digital service context for artificial structures designed to avoid tax. If the LP cannot substantiate that the supply was made to a non-resident or that consideration was received from outside Canada within a reasonable period (administratively accepted as 180 days), the zero rating is denied and GST/HST plus QST become payable, with assessed interest. Under section 285 ETA, knowingly making a false statement or evasion is subject to penalties up to 25% of the assessed amount plus fines up to CAD 50,000, and upon conviction for tax evasion, a fine up to 200% of the tax evaded and/or imprisonment up to 5 years. Revenu Québec imposes equivalent penalties under sections 1160, 1161, and 1162 of the Taxation Act and section 40 of the Tax Administration Act. Retroactive clawback may extend four years for normal assessments and indefinitely where misrepresentation is involved. Additionally, if the LP fails to register for GST/HST and QST while making taxable digital supplies to Quebec consumers, it may be assessed for uncollected taxes under section 323 ETA, plus penalties for failure to register.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); monetary authority with no statutory exchange-control mandate. Cross-border currency reporting and AML/ATF monitoring are administered by FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada), not by a separate foreign-exchange administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility. No foreign-exchange permits, nationality restrictions, or prior approvals apply to capital injections, dividend payments, partnership distributions, or profit remittances. For a Quebec Limited Partnership, a non-resident partner carrying on business in Canada through the LP may be taxable on the Canadian-source partnership income, and treaty-based allocation rules under the Canada-US or other applicable tax treaties must be observed. Part XIII withholding may apply to remittances characterized as interest, royalties, or deemed periodic payments, but such fiscal frictions are tax obligations, not currency-control restrictions. The principal practical barriers are bank KYC/EDD, source-of-funds substantiation, and sanctions compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender rules, mandated conversion timelines, or minimum conversion ratios exist in Canada. Export proceeds may be retained indefinitely in foreign currency and used freely for operational or treasury purposes. Reporting obligations apply only through anti-money-laundering channels: any incoming or outgoing wire transfer of C$10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC, and all export receipts must be supported by records sufficient for Canadian income tax and GST/QST purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium in Quebec. Foreign fintech EMIs are not recognized as domestic banking institutions under Canadian law; they cannot accept deposits or act as cash custodians without registration or bank sponsorship. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act, payment service providers performing core retail payment functions in Canada are required to register with the Bank of Canada. Foreign EMIs must therefore either establish a Canadian registered entity and obtain the applicable regulatory authorization, or operate through a Tier 1 Canadian bank sponsor. For this LP, foreign digital EMIs should be used solely as SaaS subscription merchant gateways (e.g., Stripe, Paymentwall, or PayPal) and never as primary treasury collateral or liquidity providers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid. Remote account opening is possible at most Schedule I banks only for low-risk structures with wholly domestic ownership and a simple UBO chain. For a Medium-Risk VPN/SaaS Quebec LP with non-resident limited partners, enhanced due diligence under FINTRAC rules will require a physical or video-verified compliance interview with at least one general partner or designated signing officer. Quebec branches frequently require an in-person meeting for the opening signatory at a Montreal or Toronto corporate banking centre; notarized corporate documents, original LP registration evidence, partnership agreement, and identity/source-of-funds documentation for all 25% or greater beneficial owners are mandatory before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque UBO chain through LP units or layered trust ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Register of Individuals with Significant Control, executed partnership agreement with capital contribution schedule, ledger of limited partner identities and percentage allocations, source-of-funds bank statements, Quebec Registraire des entreprises extract or Individual Partner Certificate, and notarized identity documents for all beneficial owners in the chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: VPN and privacy-software product flagged in adverse media or sanctions screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINTRAC-compliant AML/ATF compliance program, sanctions and PEP screening logs, technical product whitepaper, acceptable-use and anti-fraud policies, marketing and privacy-policy materials, OFAC/EU/UN sanctions filter results, and external counsel legal opinion on encryption, data collection, and lawful interception requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment volumes inconsistent with a subscription SaaS revenue model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subscriber dashboard and daily/monthly recurring revenue reports, payment processor settlement statements from Stripe and Paymentwall, invoicing and billing-metering exports, bank statements reconciled to sales records, and filed corporate income tax and GST/QST returns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partner located in a FATF high-risk or higher-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence questionnaire, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, notarized passport and proof of address, independent third-party KYC/EDD report, beneficial ownership attestations, and a sworn declaration of tax residence and beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from an offshore entity with unclear commercial purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call notice, executed subscription agreement, LP capital account statement, general partner resolution, remitter KYC declaration, source-of-funds bank statements, and the SWIFT MT103 confirmation with the remittance reference 'LP capital contribution'.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SWIFT MT103 wire from the non-resident investor's bank to the LP's Tier 1 Canadian bank account in Montreal or Toronto. The remittance advice must state 'LP capital contribution / partnership capital call' and reference the applicable capital call number. No Bank of Canada or FINTRAC prior approval is required, but the receiving bank will require the executed capital call, a partnership agreement extract showing capital account mechanics, source-of-funds evidence, and FINTRAC EFT reporting for any transaction of C$10,000 or more. Canada does not use mandatory SWIFT purpose codes; descriptive wire text containing the corporate entity name, LP account number, and capital contribution identifier is customary. If a US investor is remitting, the bank may also require IRS Form W-9 or W-8BEN-E for Client Identification and information reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for invoiced vendor and licensor payments, MT202 COV for interbank or correspondent clearing of higher-value disbursements, and commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) for hardware, infrastructure, or trust-priced procurement contracts. Each outbound payment must be mapped to a valid purchase order or licence invoice, and Part XIII withholding must be assessed for Canadian-source payments to non-residents, including royalty, service, or infrastructure fees, to avoid CRA penalties. CAD and USD dual-currency clearing accounts at the Tier 1 bank reduce redundant conversions and align funding with North American settlement windows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX contracts for immediate settlement of vendor obligations
Vanilla deliverable FX forwards in CAD/USD and CAD/EUR for budget-rate certainty
Non-deliverable forwards where counterparties require USD cash settlement or where exposure to a restricted or non-deliverable emerging-market currency arises
Cross-currency swaps under an ISDA Master Agreement for long-term balance-sheet hedging
Exchange-traded FX futures and options, subject to corporate account approvals and harmonized clearing and margin requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Update Declaration (Déclaration annuelle de mise à jour) — mandatory registration renewal for the limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) / Quebec Business Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due during the month preceding the LP's registration anniversary (e.g., registration on 15 July requires filing from 1 June through 30 June); based on the REQ-assigned immatriculation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge approximately CAD $27.25 (~USD $20); persistent default past one year triggers automatic strike-off and dissolution of the enterprise's registration; continued operation without registration exposes the general partner to penal fines up to CAD $15,000 (corporate) or CAD $3,000 (individual) plus loss of legal publicity effects

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return — annual allocation of income, losses, and capital items to all partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following a December 31 fiscal period; for non-calendar fiscal periods, within 5 months after the fiscal period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD $25 per day (minimum CAD $100, maximum CAD $2,500); tax-shelter partnerships face CAD $25 per day per investor without the standard cap; partner loss claims may be suspended until the return is filed; gross-negligence penalties apply under the Income Tax Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec provincial partnership annual information schedule and allocation slips for Quebec-resident partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the federal T5013 deadline (March 31 for a December 31 fiscal period); partners must receive Quebec allocation slips by the last day of February following the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% plus 1% per full month up to 12% of any assessed balance; missing allocation slips trigger fines of CAD $10–$25 per slip (minimum CAD $100 per return) and penal prosecution for repeated non-compliance under the Tax Administration Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit for a Quebec Société en commandite under the Civil Code of Quebec or the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. An independent audit is required only if the limited partnership agreement stipulates it, the LP becomes a reporting issuer under the Quebec Securities Act through public unit distribution, or a debt or investor covenant mandates audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS if the LP or its consolidated group is publicly accountable; otherwise ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) is permissible for private LPs. The CRA/Revenu Québec schedules follow the Income Tax Act allocation of income, and the REQ transparency regime may require additional financial data for qualifying large enterprises.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Effective 31 March 2023, the REQ ultimate beneficiary regime requires the general partner to identify all natural persons who, directly or indirectly, own or control 25% or more of the LP's rights (profit shares, capital interests, or voting rights of the general partner). The annual update declaration must re-certify UBO data each anniversary; assignments or transfers of limited partnership interests and any change in control of the general partner must be reported as material changes within 15 days. Willful omission triggers penal fines up to CAD $15,000 for corporations and CAD $3,000 for individuals, plus suspension of the certificate of registration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (capital contributions, profit-share entitlements, and contact details)
Register of Transfers and Assignments of Partnership Interests (with dates and consents)
Minute Book of General Partner Resolutions and Unanimous Partner Consents (including partnership agreement amendments)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 185–735 per year (CAD 250–1,000) depending on the corporate secretarial provider and Quebec registered-office address service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,700–18,400 per engagement year (CAD 5,000–25,000) for a private-company-scale VPN/SaaS limited partnership if an audit or attestation engagement is contractually required

stage_6.entry_description: Legal name, business number (BN), mailing address, fiscal period end, business activity code (NAICS 2022 517919 for VPN/digital security software)
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: State country of residence of every non-resident partner; attach Schedule for non-resident allocation; provide address outside Canada
